What is FitTrack?

FitTrack is a free fitness tracker that runs in one web page — no sign-up, no cost. It logs your workouts and estimates calories burned, charts your body weight against your goal, counts daily water up to 4 litres, calculates your BMI and daily calorie needs, tracks sleep and daily steps, and saves your personal lifting records. Everything is counted live from your own entries and saved in your browser, and you can export it all as CSV or JSON whenever you want.

    Calculator

    BMI & daily calories

    Enter your numbers and hit Calculate. Uses the standard BMI and Mifflin-St Jeor formulas.

    BMI 19.4 · Healthy

    Maintenance ≈ 2,610 kcal/day · To gain muscle slowly, aim ≈ 2,860 kcal/day with ~95 g protein.

    How to read it

    Under 18.5 — Underweight. Eat in a small surplus and lift progressively.

    18.5 – 24.9 — Healthy range. Best zone for building muscle while staying lean.

    25 – 29.9 — Overweight. A small deficit + strength training works well.

    30 + — Obese range. Start with walking, food habits and a clinician's advice.

    Protein rule of thumb: about 1.6 g per kg of body weight per day for muscle gain — roughly 95 g at 59.5 kg.

        Questions

        Frequently asked questions

        Straight answers about how FitTrack works, how its numbers are calculated, and what happens to your data.

        What is FitTrack?
        FitTrack is a free fitness tracker that runs in a single web page. It logs workouts and estimates calories burned, charts body weight against a 60 kg goal, counts daily water up to 4 litres, calculates BMI and daily calorie needs, tracks sleep and daily steps, and saves personal lifting records — with no sign-up and no cost.
        How do I log a workout?
        Go to the Log a Workout section, type the workout name, choose its type, enter the duration in minutes, pick the intensity, and press Add to log. Calories are estimated as minutes × intensity — about 6 kcal/min light, 9 moderate, 12 hard — and the dashboard, streak, weekly goal and 7-day chart all update instantly.
        How is BMI calculated here?
        BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². A BMI of 18.5–24.9 is the healthy range. The calculator also estimates daily calories with the Mifflin-St Jeor formula (10 × weight + 6.25 × height − 5 × age + 5, times your activity level) and suggests about 1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight for muscle gain.
        How much water should I drink a day?
        FitTrack's goal is 16 glasses ≈ 4 litres a day, set for someone who plays football and trains in the gym on the same day. Tap a glass in the Water Tracker each time you drink one — the counter resets to zero every new day so each morning starts honest.
        How much sleep do I need to recover?
        Most active adults recover best on 7 to 9 hours. The Sleep & Recovery section scores each night out of 100 from hours slept and sleep quality: 85+ means go hard, 60–84 train as planned, and under 60 is a sign to swap the heavy session for mobility or a walk.
        How many steps should I take a day?
        FitTrack's default goal is 10,000 steps a day, and you can change it in the Step Counter. Enter steps from your phone in chunks as the day goes; the total resets each morning. A 10-minute walk is roughly 1,000 steps.
        Is FitTrack free? Where is my data saved?
        Yes — 100% free, no sign-up. Your workouts, weigh-ins, water, sleep, steps and records are saved only in your own browser on your device. Download a CSV spreadsheet or JSON backup any time from the Advanced Tracking section.
